class: JSON responses whose ip value contains four decimal octets in the range 0–255, with at least one octet padded with leading zeros.
rule_a: If the address contains four decimal octets in the range 0–255 but any multi-digit octet begins with zero, return 'Invalid IP address received'.
rule_b: If the address contains four decimal octets in the range 0–255 but any multi-digit octet begins with zero, return the address unchanged.

class: Numeric DataFrames containing NaN values after replacement, with enough jointly observed values to calculate each pairwise correlation.
rule_a: If any column contains NaN values after replacement, calculate each correlation, including self-correlations, using only rows where both participating columns have non-NaN values.
rule_b: If any column contains NaN values after replacement, set every correlation involving that column, including its self-correlation, to NaN and calculate correlations between unaffected columns normally.

class: Inputs with precision 2 whose rounded square roots require trailing-zero padding to display exactly two fractional digits.
rule_a: When precision is 2, encode the rounded square root as a JSON string with exactly two digits after the decimal point.
rule_b: When precision is 2, encode the rounded square root as a JSON string without trailing fractional zeros, except that whole-number results retain one fractional zero.

class: DataFrames whose selected column changes under label encoding, making modification of the caller's DataFrame observable.
rule_a: Return a DataFrame with the requested column encoded while leaving the supplied DataFrame unchanged.
rule_b: Replace the requested column in the supplied DataFrame with its encoding and return that same DataFrame.

class: DataFrames whose rows are not already ordered by ascending id, leaving the returned row order unspecified.
rule_a: Return standardized rows in their original input order, even when different ids are interleaved.
rule_b: Return standardized rows grouped by ascending id, preserving their original input order within each group.

class: Column strings containing leading, trailing, or non-single-space whitespace when the pattern is nonempty.
rule_a: For a nonempty pattern, preserve the exact leading, trailing, and between-word whitespace while reordering words.
rule_b: For a nonempty pattern, remove leading and trailing whitespace and separate reordered words with exactly one ASCII space.

class: Finite 2D numeric NumPy arrays containing at least one constant column, whose standard deviation is zero.
rule_a: For any column with zero standard deviation, return NaN in every entry of that column.
rule_b: For any column with zero standard deviation, return 0.0 in every entry of that column.

class: Rectangular numeric inputs with at least one column containing only integers and at least one column containing a float.
rule_a: If any input column contains a float, store every column of the returned data DataFrame with floating-point dtype.
rule_b: If any input column contains a float, infer each column of the returned data DataFrame independently, retaining integer dtype for columns containing only integers.

class: Numeric DataFrames whose row index differs from the default unnamed RangeIndex.
rule_a: The standardized DataFrame must preserve the input DataFrame's row index, including its labels and name.
rule_b: The standardized DataFrame must replace the input DataFrame's row index with an unnamed RangeIndex starting at zero.

class: Nested dictionaries whose surviving keys are strings and first appear in an order different from lexicographic order.
rule_a: When all remaining keys are strings, insert them into the returned dictionary in lexicographic order.
rule_b: When all remaining keys are strings, insert them into the returned dictionary in first-encounter order, traversing both the outer dictionary and each inner dictionary in insertion order.

class: Lists of integer sublists whose distinct elements first appear in a different order from ascending numerical order, leaving the returned Counter's key iteration order unspecified.
rule_a: For integer elements, the returned Counter must iterate over its keys in ascending numerical order.
rule_b: For integer elements, the returned Counter must iterate over its keys in order of first occurrence when reading the sublists from left to right.

class: DataFrames with at least two rows whose target column is constant and is fitted exactly by the regression model.
rule_a: If the target is constant and fitted exactly, return NaN because R-squared has a zero denominator.
rule_b: If the target is constant and fitted exactly, return 1.0 because the model achieves a perfect fit.

class: DataFrames whose unique column labels differ from their zero-based column positions.
rule_a: Use each column's zero-based position as the dictionary key for its Shapiro–Wilk p-value.
rule_b: Use each column's label as the dictionary key for its Shapiro–Wilk p-value.

class: Inputs for which DBSCAN finds at least two non-noise clusters, whose numeric labels require an ordering convention.
rule_a: If DBSCAN finds multiple clusters, number them consecutively from 0 in lexicographic order of each cluster's smallest feature vector, and label noise -1.
rule_b: If DBSCAN finds multiple clusters, number them consecutively from 0 in ascending order of each cluster's smallest original row index, and label noise -1.

class: Dictionaries containing multiple initial-character groups whose first-occurrence order differs from character-sorted order.
rule_a: Insert aggregated groups into the returned dictionary in the order their initial characters first appear in the input dictionary.
rule_b: Insert aggregated groups into the returned dictionary in ascending order of their initial characters.

class: Nonempty lists whose values are all equal, so the min-max scaling denominator is zero.
rule_a: If all values in a nonempty list are equal, return a one-dimensional ndarray of the same length filled with 0.5.
rule_b: If all values in a nonempty list are equal, return a one-dimensional ndarray of the same length filled with 0.0.

class: Comma-separated strings containing fields that mix words and unsigned numeric tokens separated by spaces.
rule_a: For fields that mix words and unsigned numeric tokens separated by spaces, exclude all numeric tokens from both the count and the square-root sum.
rule_b: For fields that mix words and unsigned numeric tokens separated by spaces, include all numeric tokens in both the count and the square-root sum.

class: Nonempty lists whose values are all Python booleans and include both True and False.
rule_a: If every value is a boolean and both truth values occur, raise ValueError because boolean values are not considered numeric.
rule_b: If every value is a boolean and both truth values occur, return the DataFrame with False normalized to 0.0 and True normalized to 1.0.

skip: Letter values and multiplication determine the result, including repeated letters, and the empty list has the standard empty product of 1.

class: Text containing hyphens between letters, where punctuation removal could either join the adjacent text or separate it into words.
rule_a: Replace each hyphen between letters with a space before removing stopwords.
rule_b: Delete each hyphen between letters without inserting a space before removing stopwords.

class: Texts containing base letters followed by Unicode combining marks, for which a character can mean either a Unicode code point or a combined written character.
rule_a: After excluding whitespace and string.punctuation, treat each base letter together with its following combining marks as one character for both character counts, with uniqueness determined by exact sequences.
rule_b: After excluding whitespace and string.punctuation, treat each base letter and each following combining mark as separate characters for both character counts, with uniqueness determined by individual Unicode code points.

class: Dictionaries whose retained animal keys occur in a different order from ANIMAL and produce letters with equal frequencies.
rule_a: For letters with equal frequencies, order them by first appearance when reading retained animal names left to right in ANIMAL order.
rule_b: For letters with equal frequencies, order them by first appearance when reading retained animal names left to right in dictionary insertion order.

class: Inputs containing an inner list longer than the ten-element predefined range.
rule_a: If any inner list has more than ten elements, raise ValueError because the predefined range contains too few elements.
rule_b: If an inner list has more than ten elements, use all ten elements of the predefined range once to calculate its sum of squares.

class: Numeric 2D arrays containing repeated values, for which uniqueness may refer to pairs of positions or pairs of values.
rule_a: When values repeat, enumerate pairs of distinct positions in the sorted array in lexicographic position order, retaining only the first occurrence of each resulting value pair.
rule_b: When values repeat, enumerate pairs of distinct positions in the sorted array in lexicographic position order, retaining every resulting value pair even when it duplicates an earlier pair.
